items.q: A hollow conducting sphere of radius R has charge Q. If the radius is doubled keeping charge same, the electric flux through the Gaussian surface enclosing the sphere will:
items.key: Electric flux depends only on enclosed charge (Gauss's Law: Φ = Q/ε₀), not on size of Gaussian surface.

items.q: Two heaters, each rated 1000 W at 220 V, are connected in parallel across a 220 V supply. Total power consumed is:
items.key: In parallel each heater gets its rated 220 V, so each consumes 1000 W. Total P = 1000 + 1000 = 2000 W.

items.q: A solid metallic cylinder is placed in a uniform magnetic field with its axis parallel to the field. If the field changes with time, the induced (eddy) currents in the cylinder flow:
opts: B. in circular paths around its axis
C. nowhere — no current is induced
D. only along the curved surface, parallel to the axis
items.key: Flux through every circular loop perpendicular to the axis changes, so an emf is induced around such loops. Eddy currents therefore circulate in circles about the axis (Faraday–Lenz).

items.q: An electromagnetic wave propagating along x-axis has equation E = E₀cos(kx−ωt). Direction of propagation is:
items.key: Direction of EM wave propagation is along +x̂ (given by k direction in kx−ωt).

items.q: Which of the following cannot be explained by Huygens' wave theory of light?
items.key: Huygens' principle explains reflection, refraction, interference, diffraction — but NOT origin of spectra (needs quantum theory).

items.q: A distant star sends light to Earth. The wavefront reaching Earth is:
items.key: Star is so far that wavefront is essentially plane by the time it reaches Earth.

items.q: The binding energy per nucleon is maximum for nuclei near iron (Fe-56). This means these nuclei:
opts: D. cannot participate in nuclear reactions
items.key: Maximum binding energy per nucleon = maximum stability = most tightly bound nuclei.

items.q: A small bismuth rod is suspended freely between the poles of a strong electromagnet that produces a non-uniform field. The rod will:
opts: A. align along the field and move towards the stronger field
B. not be affected at all
D. align perpendicular to the field and move towards the weaker field
items.key: Bismuth is diamagnetic (χ small and negative): it is weakly repelled, so it settles across the field and tends to move from stronger to weaker field regions.

items.q: In a Wheatstone bridge, arms AB = 2 Ω, BC = 4 Ω, AD = 3 Ω and DC = 6 Ω. A 5 Ω galvanometer is connected between B and D and an 18 V battery of negligible internal resistance between A and C. Current drawn from the battery is:
items.key: AB/BC = 2/4 = AD/DC = 3/6 → bridge balanced, no current through galvanometer. R_AC = (2+4)(3+6)/(6+9) = 54/15 = 3.6 Ω. I = 18/3.6 = 5 A.

items.q: Resistances R₁ and R₂ dissipate power P₁=60W and P₂=100W from same supply. R₁:R₂ =
items.key: R = V²/P, so R₁/R₂ = P₂/P₁ = 100/60 = 5:3.

items.q: The size of a nucleus is about 10⁻¹⁵ m. If a football (22 cm radius) represents the nucleus, size of atom would be:
items.key: Atom/nucleus ratio ~10⁵. 0.22 m × 10⁵ = 22,000 m = 22 km.

items.q: A circular loop of radius 0.1 m carries current 5 A. Magnetic field at centre:
[A-R Q13] A: Most of the α particles pass undeflected through gold foil. R: Most of the space in atom is empty.
opts: A. Both A and R true, R explains A
B. Both true, R not correct explanation
items.key: Both true, and R explains A: the atom is mostly empty space with a tiny nucleus, so most α-particles never come close to the nucleus and pass undeflected.

items.q: [A-R Q14] A: A convex lens submerged in water has greater focal length. R: Lens formula uses relative refractive index.
opts: A. Both A and R true, R explains A
B. Both true, R not correct explanation
items.key: Both true, R correctly explains A: in water relative μ decreases, so power decreases, focal length increases.

items.q: [A-R Q15] A: In YDSE, decreasing slit separation increases fringe width. R: Fringe width is directly proportional to slit separation.
opts: A. Both A and R true, R explains A
B. Both true, R not correct explanation
items.key: A is true (β = λD/d, d↓ → β↑). R is false (β is INVERSELY proportional to d).

items.q: [A-R Q16] A: Net electric field inside a conductor is zero. R: Electrons in a conductor are always stationary.
opts: A. Both A and R true, R explains A
B. Both true, R not correct explanation
items.key: A is true for a conductor in electrostatic equilibrium (free charges rearrange until E inside = 0). R is false — free electrons are in constant random thermal motion; there is just no net drift.

items.q: An electric dipole of moment 4×10⁻⁹ C m is placed in a uniform electric field of 5×10⁴ N/C with its axis at 30° to the field. The torque on the dipole is:
A 4 μF capacitor is charged to a potential difference of 50 V. The energy stored in it is:
A uniform metal wire of resistivity ρ and resistance R is cut into two equal halves, and the halves are joined in parallel. The resistivity of the material of the combination is:
items.key: Resistivity depends only on the material and temperature, not on dimensions. (The resistance changes to R/4, but ρ stays the same.)

items.q: A proton and an α-particle enter a uniform magnetic field with the same velocity, perpendicular to the field. The ratio of the radii of their circular paths, r_p : r_α, is:
items.key: r = mv/(qB). For α: m = 4m_p, q = 2e → r_α = (4m_p v)/(2eB) = 2r_p. So r_p : r_α = 1 : 2.

items.q: The magnetic susceptibility of a paramagnetic salt is 2.4×10⁻⁵ at 300 K. Its susceptibility at 200 K will be:
A bar magnet is dropped, north pole downward, along the axis of a horizontal copper ring. While the magnet is approaching the ring, the induced current in the ring, as seen from above, is:
opts: D. clockwise first and then anticlockwise
items.key: By Lenz's law the ring opposes the approaching N pole by making its upper face a north pole; a north face seen from the viewer's side has anticlockwise current.

items.q: A series AC circuit has a resistance of 30 Ω and an inductive reactance of 40 Ω (no capacitor). The power factor of the circuit is:
items.key: Z = √(30² + 40²) = 50 Ω. Power factor cos φ = R/Z = 30/50 = 0.6.

items.q: Which of the following lists electromagnetic radiations in order of increasing wavelength?
opts: B. X-rays, γ-rays, infrared, radio waves
D. ultraviolet, visible, X-rays, radio waves
items.key: Increasing wavelength: γ-rays → X-rays → UV → visible → IR → microwaves → radio waves. Only option A follows this order.

items.q: A concave mirror of focal length 15 cm forms a real image three times the size of the object. The object is placed in front of the mirror at a distance of:
items.key: Real image: m = −v/u = −3 → v = 3u. 1/v + 1/u = 1/f → 4/(3u) = 1/(−15) → u = −20 cm, i.e. 20 cm in front.

items.q: An electron and a proton have the same kinetic energy. Which of them has the larger de Broglie wavelength?
opts: B. both have the same wavelength
D. it depends on the sign of the charge
items.key: λ = h/p = h/√(2mK). For equal K, smaller mass gives larger λ. The electron is ~1836 times lighter, so its λ is larger.

items.q: The ionisation energy of a hydrogen atom in its ground state is 13.6 eV. The energy needed to excite it from n = 1 to n = 3 is:
In a reverse-biased p-n junction diode (below breakdown), the small current that flows is mainly due to:
opts: B. movement of the fixed ions of the depletion region
C. drift of minority carriers across the junction
items.key: Reverse bias raises the barrier and stops majority-carrier diffusion. Only thermally generated minority carriers are swept across by the junction field, giving a tiny (μA) current.

items.q: [A-R Q13] A: Light from two separate sodium lamps does not produce a sustained interference pattern. R: The two lamps emit light of different wavelengths.
opts: A. Both A and R true, R explains A
B. Both true, R not correct explanation
items.key: A is true. R is false — both lamps emit the same wavelength (589 nm), but they are independent sources whose phase difference changes randomly and rapidly, so they are not coherent.

items.q: [A-R Q14] A: The mass of a nucleus is always less than the sum of the masses of its free nucleons. R: When nucleons combine to form a nucleus, energy equivalent to the mass defect is released.
opts: A. Both A and R true, R explains A
B. Both true, R not correct explanation
items.key: Both true and R explains A: binding energy is released on formation (E = Δm c²), so the bound nucleus has less mass than the separate nucleons.

items.q: [A-R Q15] A: Kirchhoff's junction rule is based on conservation of charge. R: Kirchhoff's loop rule is based on conservation of energy.
opts: A. Both A and R true, R explains A
B. Both true, R not correct explanation
items.key: Both statements are true, but R describes the loop rule and does not explain the junction rule in A.

items.q: [A-R Q16] A: A ray of light passing through the optical centre of a thin lens suffers a large deviation. R: Near the optical centre the two faces of a thin lens are nearly parallel, like a thin glass slab.
opts: A. Both A and R true, R explains A
B. Both true, R not correct explanation
items.key: A is false — a ray through the optical centre goes undeviated (only a negligible lateral shift). R is true and is the reason for this.

items.q: Two point charges in air repel each other with a force F. If the space between them is filled with a medium of dielectric constant 4 and the distance between them is halved, the force becomes:
A 6 μF capacitor charged to 100 V is connected across an uncharged 3 μF capacitor. The common potential after charge sharing is:
items.key: Charge is conserved: V = C₁V₁/(C₁ + C₂) = (6 × 100)/9 ≈ 66.7 V.

items.q: The I–V graphs of the same metallic wire are drawn at two temperatures T₁ and T₂. Both are straight lines through the origin, and the line for T₁ is steeper (larger slope, I on y-axis). Then:
opts: A. T₁ is higher than T₂
C. T₁ is lower than T₂
D. the temperatures cannot be compared
items.key: Slope of I–V graph = 1/R. Steeper line → smaller R. Resistance of a metal increases with temperature, so T₁ is the lower temperature.

items.q: A circular coil of 20 turns and radius 5 cm carries a current of 1.5 A. The magnitude of its magnetic dipole moment is about:
The net magnetic flux through any closed surface placed in a magnetic field is:
opts: D. μ₀ times the pole strength enclosed
items.key: Gauss's law for magnetism: ∮B·dS = 0. Magnetic field lines form closed loops and isolated magnetic poles (monopoles) do not exist.

items.q: A coil of inductance 50 mH carries a steady current of 4 A. The energy stored in its magnetic field is:
The reactance of a capacitor is 200 Ω at 50 Hz. At 200 Hz its reactance will be:
items.key: X_C = 1/(2πfC) ∝ 1/f. Frequency becomes 4 times → X_C = 200/4 = 50 Ω.

items.q: Displacement current exists in the gap between the plates of a capacitor:
opts: A. only when the capacitor is fully charged
B. only while the electric field between the plates is changing
C. always, even with steady DC after charging
D. only if a dielectric is placed between the plates
items.key: I_d = ε₀ dΦ_E/dt. It is non-zero only while the electric flux (field) between the plates changes, i.e. during charging/discharging or with AC.

items.q: A coin lies at the bottom of a tank filled with water (μ = 4/3) to a depth of 24 cm. When viewed from directly above, the coin appears to be raised by:
items.key: Apparent depth = real depth/μ = 24 × 3/4 = 18 cm. Apparent rise = 24 − 18 = 6 cm.

items.q: The energy of a photon of wavelength 620 nm is about:
items.key: E = hc/λ ≈ 1240 eV nm/620 nm = 2.0 eV.

items.q: The ratio of the nuclear densities of ¹²C and ²⁰⁸Pb is approximately:
items.key: R = R₀A^(1/3) → volume ∝ A, and mass ∝ A, so density is independent of A. Nuclear density is the same (~2.3×10¹⁷ kg/m³) for all nuclei.

items.q: At absolute zero (0 K), a crystal of pure silicon behaves as:
items.key: At 0 K no electron has thermal energy to cross the band gap; the valence band is full and the conduction band empty, so there are no free carriers.

items.q: [A-R Q13] A: In Bohr's model, an electron in a stationary orbit does not radiate energy. R: The angular momentum of the electron in a stationary orbit is an integral multiple of h/2π.
opts: A. Both A and R true, R explains A
B. Both true, R not correct explanation
items.key: Both are true postulates of Bohr's model, but they are separate postulates; quantisation of angular momentum (R) does not explain why the orbit is non-radiating (A).

items.q: [A-R Q14] A: Diffraction of sound is noticed easily in daily life, but diffraction of light is not. R: The wavelength of sound is comparable to the size of everyday obstacles and openings, while the wavelength of light is very much smaller.
opts: A. Both A and R true, R explains A
B. Both true, R not correct explanation
items.key: Both true and R explains A: diffraction is appreciable only when the obstacle/aperture size is comparable to the wavelength.

items.q: [A-R Q15] A: The electrostatic potential inside a charged hollow conducting sphere is zero. R: The electric field inside a charged hollow conducting sphere is zero.
opts: A. Both A and R true, R explains A
B. Both true, R not correct explanation
items.key: A is false — since E = 0 inside, the potential is constant inside and equal to its value at the surface, kQ/R (not zero). R is true.

items.q: [A-R Q16] A: Microwaves are used in RADAR systems for aircraft navigation. R: Microwaves have very long wavelengths, so they bend easily around obstacles.
opts: A. Both A and R true, R explains A
B. Both true, R not correct explanation
items.key: A is true. R is false — microwaves have short wavelengths (mm to cm), so they travel as narrow, straight beams; that is why they suit RADAR.

items.q: A charge of 3 μC is carried from one point to another on an equipotential surface that is at a potential of 50 V. The work done by the electric field is:
opts: C. 1.5×10⁻⁴ J only if the path is straight
items.key: On an equipotential surface ΔV = 0, so W = qΔV = 0, whatever the path. (The value 50 V of the surface does not matter, only the potential difference.)

items.q: A parallel plate air capacitor stays connected to a battery while a slab of dielectric constant K completely fills the space between its plates. The charge on the capacitor:
items.key: With the battery connected, V stays fixed. C becomes KC₀, so Q = CV = KC₀V = K times the original charge.

items.q: A cell of emf 12 V and internal resistance 0.5 Ω supplies a current of 4 A to an external circuit. The potential difference across its terminals is:
items.key: V = E − Ir = 12 − 4 × 0.5 = 10 V (the cell is discharging, so V is less than E).

items.q: A copper wire is connected across a battery of constant potential difference. If it is replaced by another copper wire of double the length (same thickness and temperature), the drift velocity of the free electrons becomes:
items.key: v_d = eEτ/m and E = V/l. With V fixed and l doubled, E is halved, so v_d is halved.

items.q: A toroid with 400 turns has a mean radius of 10 cm and carries a current of 0.5 A. The magnetic field inside its core (air) is:
A charged particle moves through a region with only a uniform magnetic field. Which quantity of the particle remains constant?
items.key: The magnetic force q(v × B) is always perpendicular to v, so it does no work: the speed and hence kinetic energy stay constant, though the direction of velocity (and momentum) changes.

items.q: The current in a coil of self-inductance 0.3 H falls uniformly from 5 A to 1 A in 0.2 s. The magnitude of the self-induced emf is:
The instantaneous voltage of the household supply is v = 311 sin(100πt) volt. Its rms value and frequency are:
In a plane electromagnetic wave in vacuum, the amplitude of the electric field is 60 V/m. The amplitude of the magnetic field is:
When a narrow beam of white light passes through a glass prism, the colour that is deviated the least is:
items.key: Refractive index of glass is least for red (longest wavelength), and deviation increases with refractive index, so red deviates least.

items.q: A convex lens of focal length 15 cm is used to form a real image of an object on a screen. The minimum possible distance between the object and its real image is:
items.key: For a real image the object–image distance u + v is least when u = v = 2f. Minimum distance = 4f = 4 × 15 = 60 cm.

items.q: The work function of a metal is 3.1 eV. The threshold (longest) wavelength of light that can eject photoelectrons from it is about:
items.key: λ₀ = hc/φ₀ ≈ 1240 eV nm/3.1 eV = 400 nm.

items.q: [A-R Q13] A: In a hydrogen atom, the energy levels come closer and closer together as the principal quantum number n increases. R: The radius of the nth orbit is proportional to n².
opts: A. Both A and R true, R explains A
B. Both true, R not correct explanation
items.key: Both true. A follows from E_n = −13.6/n² eV (the gap between successive levels falls as n grows). R is a correct statement about orbit radii but does not explain the spacing of energy levels.

items.q: [A-R Q14] A: At room temperature, pure germanium conducts better than pure silicon. R: The band gap of germanium (about 0.7 eV) is smaller than that of silicon (about 1.1 eV).
opts: A. Both A and R true, R explains A
B. Both true, R not correct explanation
items.key: Both true and R explains A: with a smaller band gap, many more electrons are thermally excited into the conduction band of Ge, giving more electron–hole pairs and higher conductivity.

items.q: [A-R Q15] A: Total internal reflection can take place when light travels from water into glass. R: For total internal reflection, light must travel from an optically denser medium to an optically rarer medium.
opts: A. Both A and R true, R explains A
B. Both true, R not correct explanation
items.key: A is false — glass is optically denser than water, so light going from water to glass cannot be totally reflected. R is true and is the very reason A fails.

items.q: [A-R Q16] A: Nuclear forces are short-range forces. R: The nuclear force between two nucleons is attractive at all separations.
opts: A. Both A and R true, R explains A
B. Both true, R not correct explanation
items.key: A is true — the nuclear force is negligible beyond a few femtometres. R is false — the force is strongly repulsive when nucleons come closer than about 0.8 fm, and attractive only over a small range.

items.q: Two electric field lines never cross each other because:
opts: A. field lines are always straight
C. at any point the electric field has only one direction
D. field lines start only from positive charges
items.key: If two lines crossed, there would be two tangents (two directions of E) at the crossing point, which is impossible since the net field at a point is unique.

items.q: A point charge of 2 nC is fixed in air. The work needed to bring a charge of 3 μC from infinity to a point 30 cm from it is:
Five identical resistors, each of resistance R, are first connected in series and then in parallel. The ratio of the equivalent resistance in series to that in parallel is:
items.key: R_series = 5R, R_parallel = R/5. Ratio = 5R ÷ (R/5) = 25 : 1.

items.q: When the temperature of a metallic conductor is increased, the average relaxation time of its free electrons:
opts: D. first increases and then decreases
items.key: At higher temperature the ions vibrate more strongly, so electrons collide more often; τ decreases, and resistivity ρ = m/(ne²τ) increases.

items.q: A charged particle moves in a circle perpendicular to a uniform magnetic field. If its speed is doubled, the time it takes to complete one revolution:
items.key: T = 2πm/(qB), independent of speed. Doubling v doubles the radius r = mv/(qB), but the period is unchanged.

items.q: When a ferromagnetic material such as iron is heated above its Curie temperature, it:
items.key: Above the Curie temperature thermal agitation destroys the alignment of the domains, and the material behaves as a paramagnetic substance.

items.q: A metal rod 1 m long rotates at 10 rad/s about an axis through one end, perpendicular to the rod, in a uniform magnetic field of 0.5 T parallel to the axis. The emf induced between its ends is:
An inductor of 10 mH and a capacitor of 1 μF are connected in series to an AC source. The angular frequency at which resonance occurs is:
Many household water purifiers in India use a lamp that kills bacteria in the water. The electromagnetic radiation emitted by this lamp is:
items.key: UV radiation (short wavelength, high-energy photons) damages the DNA of micro-organisms, so UV lamps are used to disinfect drinking water.

items.q: A real object is placed anywhere in front of a convex mirror. The image formed is always:
opts: C. real, erect and of the same size
items.key: For a convex mirror, f is positive and v always comes out positive and smaller than |u|, so the image is behind the mirror (virtual), erect and diminished.

items.q: A thin glass lens (μ = 1.5) is completely immersed in a transparent liquid that also has refractive index 1.5. Inside the liquid the lens:
opts: A. behaves like a plane glass sheet (zero power)
B. has the same focal length as in air
C. has its focal length doubled
D. changes from converging to diverging
items.key: Lens maker's formula: 1/f = (μ_g/μ_l − 1)(1/R₁ − 1/R₂) = (1 − 1)(…) = 0. So f is infinite and the power is zero — the lens becomes practically invisible.

items.q: In a Young's double-slit experiment, the intensity of light from one slit is four times that from the other. The ratio of maximum to minimum intensity in the interference pattern is:
items.key: Amplitudes are in the ratio √4 : 1 = 2 : 1. I_max/I_min = (2 + 1)²/(2 − 1)² = 9 : 1.

items.q: [A-R Q13] A: According to Bohr's model, the electron in a hydrogen atom moves faster in an inner orbit than in an outer orbit. R: The speed of the electron in the nth orbit is inversely proportional to n.
opts: A. Both A and R true, R explains A
B. Both true, R not correct explanation
items.key: Both true and R explains A: v_n = e²/(2ε₀nh) ∝ 1/n, so the speed is greatest in n = 1 and decreases outwards.

items.q: [A-R Q14] A: For light above the threshold frequency, the photoelectric current increases when the intensity of light is increased. R: The stopping potential increases when the intensity of light is increased.
opts: A. Both A and R true, R explains A
B. Both true, R not correct explanation
items.key: A is true — more photons per second eject more electrons. R is false — the stopping potential depends only on the frequency of light (and the metal), not on intensity.

items.q: [A-R Q15] A: When a p-n junction is formed, holes diffuse from the n-side to the p-side. R: The concentration of holes is much higher on the p-side than on the n-side.
opts: A. Both A and R true, R explains A
B. Both true, R not correct explanation
items.key: A is false — holes diffuse from the p-side (high concentration) to the n-side (low concentration). R is true and shows why the direction in A is wrong.

items.q: [A-R Q16] A: The binding energy per nucleon is nearly the same for nuclei with mass numbers between about 30 and 170. R: The nuclear force between two nucleons is independent of their charge.
opts: A. Both A and R true, R explains A
B. Both true, R not correct explanation
items.key: Both statements are true, but the near-constancy of BE/A is explained by the short range (saturation) of the nuclear force — each nucleon interacts only with its nearest neighbours — not by its charge independence.

items.q: An EM wave has frequency ν = 10¹⁸ Hz and travels in vacuum. Find: (i) refractive index of medium if speed is 2×10⁸ m/s, (ii) angular frequency ω.
items.ans:
(i) μ = c/v = 3×10⁸/2×10⁸ = 1.5
(ii) ω = 2πν = 2π×10¹⁸ rad/s; frequency corresponds to X-ray range.

items.q: Distinguish between path of free electrons in a conductor (a) with electric field applied, (b) without electric field.
items.ans:
(a) With E-field: electrons drift opposite to E (superimposed on random motion) → net current flows.
(b) Without E-field: purely random thermal motion; no net displacement → no current.

items.q: Two equal positive charges +q are placed at distance d apart. Find potential and work done to bring charge +q from infinity to midpoint.
Relative permeability of a material is 800. Identify type and state any two properties.
items.ans:
Type: Ferromagnetic (μr >> 1).
Properties: (1) Strongly attracted by magnetic field. (2) Can retain magnetism after field removed (hysteresis).

items.q: An AC source with frequency 50 Hz is connected to an inductor. If current lags voltage by 90°, explain why? Find reactance if L = 2 H.
items.ans:
In pure inductor, current lags voltage by 90° due to back-emf opposing change in current.
X_L = 2πfL = 2π×50×2 = 200π ≈ 628 Ω.

items.q: Two point charges +5 μC and −3 μC are placed 40 cm apart in air. Find the points on the line joining them where the electric potential is zero.
items.ans:
Let the point be at distance x from +5 μC. V = k(5/x − 3/r₂) = 0 → 5/x = 3/r₂.
Between the charges (r₂ = 0.40 − x): 5(0.40 − x) = 3x → x = 0.25 m, i.e. 25 cm from +5 μC (15 cm from −3 μC). [1]
Outside, beyond −3 μC (r₂ = x − 0.40): 5(x − 0.40) = 3x → x = 1.0 m, i.e. 60 cm beyond the −3 μC charge. [1]

items.q: A galvanometer of resistance 40 Ω gives full-scale deflection for a current of 2 mA. How will you convert it into a voltmeter of range 0–10 V? What is the resistance of the voltmeter so formed?
items.ans:
Connect a high resistance R in series: R = V/I_g − G = 10/(2×10⁻³) − 40 = 5000 − 40 = 4960 Ω. [1]
Resistance of voltmeter = G + R = 5000 Ω (high, so it draws little current). [1]

items.q: In Young's double-slit experiment, light of wavelength 600 nm is used, the slits are 0.3 mm apart and the screen is 1.5 m away. Find (i) the fringe width, (ii) the distance of the third dark fringe from the central bright fringe.
Light of wavelength 400 nm falls on a metal surface of work function 2.3 eV. Find (i) the maximum kinetic energy of the emitted photoelectrons, (ii) the stopping potential.
Explain how the depletion region and the barrier potential are formed in a p-n junction.
items.ans:
When the junction is formed, electrons diffuse from n-side to p-side and holes from p-side to n-side (concentration difference). They leave behind immobile positive donor ions on the n-side and negative acceptor ions on the p-side near the junction — this layer, free of mobile carriers, is the depletion region. [1]
These ions set up an electric field from n to p that opposes further diffusion and causes drift of minority carriers. At equilibrium diffusion current = drift current; the potential difference across the depletion layer is the barrier potential (≈ 0.7 V for Si, 0.3 V for Ge). [1]

items.q: A point charge of 1.77 μC is placed at the centre of a cube of side 10 cm. Find (i) the total electric flux through the cube, (ii) the flux through one face of the cube. (ε₀ = 8.85×10⁻¹² C² N⁻¹ m⁻²)
items.ans:
(i) By Gauss's law Φ = q/ε₀ = 1.77×10⁻⁶/8.85×10⁻¹² = 2.0×10⁵ N m² C⁻¹ (independent of the cube's size). [1]
(ii) By symmetry each of the 6 faces gets equal flux: Φ_face = 2.0×10⁵/6 ≈ 3.33×10⁴ N m² C⁻¹. [1]

items.q: Pure silicon has an intrinsic carrier concentration of 1.5×10¹⁶ m⁻³. It is doped with arsenic so that the free-electron concentration becomes 3×10²² m⁻³. Find the hole concentration and state the type of semiconductor formed.
items.ans:
n_e n_h = n_i² → n_h = (1.5×10¹⁶)²/(3×10²²) = 2.25×10³²/3×10²² = 7.5×10⁹ m⁻³. [1]
Since n_e ≫ n_h (arsenic is pentavalent, a donor), it is an n-type semiconductor. [1]

items.q: The current in a coil changes steadily from 2 A to 6 A in 0.05 s, and an emf of 0.8 V is induced in a neighbouring coil. Find (i) the mutual inductance of the pair, (ii) the change in flux linkage with the second coil.
A convex lens of focal length 20 cm is placed in contact with a concave lens of focal length 30 cm. Find the power and focal length of the combination, and state its nature.
items.ans:
P = P₁ + P₂ = 100/20 + 100/(−30) = 5 − 3.33 ≈ +1.67 D. [1]
f = 1/P = 100/1.67 cm = 60 cm; positive power → the combination behaves as a converging (convex) lens. [1]

items.q: An electron is accelerated from rest through a potential difference of 150 V. Calculate its de Broglie wavelength. In which region of the electromagnetic spectrum does a photon of this wavelength lie?
items.ans:
λ = h/√(2meV) = 6.63×10⁻³⁴/√(2 × 9.11×10⁻³¹ × 1.6×10⁻¹⁹ × 150) ≈ 1.0×10⁻¹⁰ m (or λ = 1.227/√V nm = 0.100 nm). [1]
λ ≈ 0.1 nm = 1 Å, which lies in the X-ray region (comparable to inter-atomic spacing). [1]

items.q: Two wires A and B are made of the same metal. B is twice as long as A and has twice its diameter. Find the ratio of their resistances. If they are connected in series across a battery, find the ratio of the powers dissipated in A and B.
items.ans:
R = ρl/A = 4ρl/(πd²), so R ∝ l/d². R_B/R_A = 2/2² = 1/2 → R_A : R_B = 2 : 1. [1]
In series the same current flows, so P = I²R ∝ R → P_A : P_B = 2 : 1. [1]

items.q: A straight wire 0.5 m long carrying a current of 3 A is placed in a uniform magnetic field of 0.4 T, the wire making an angle of 30° with the field. Find the force on the wire. At what angle would this force be maximum, and what would be its value?
items.ans:
F = BIl sin θ = 0.4 × 3 × 0.5 × sin 30° = 0.3 N, perpendicular to the plane containing the wire and B (Fleming's left-hand rule). [1]
Maximum when the wire is perpendicular to the field (θ = 90°): F_max = BIl = 0.4 × 3 × 0.5 = 0.6 N. [1]

items.q: A ray of light is incident at 60° on the surface of a glass slab of refractive index √3. Find the angle of refraction and show that the reflected and refracted rays are perpendicular to each other.
items.ans:
Snell's law: sin r = sin 60°/√3 = (√3/2)/√3 = 1/2 → r = 30°. [1]
Reflected ray makes 60° with the normal and the refracted ray 30° on the other side, so the angle between them = 180° − 60° − 30° = 90°. [1]

items.q: A proton and an α-particle are each accelerated from rest through the same potential difference. Find the ratio of their de Broglie wavelengths, λ_p : λ_α.
Give two differences between intrinsic and extrinsic semiconductors. Why does doping silicon with a trivalent impurity produce a p-type semiconductor?
items.ans:
Intrinsic: pure, n_e = n_h, very low conductivity at room temperature. Extrinsic: doped with impurity, n_e ≠ n_h, much higher and controllable conductivity. [1]
A trivalent atom (B, Al, Ga, In) forms only three covalent bonds with neighbouring Si atoms; the vacancy in the fourth bond is a hole, which can accept an electron. So holes become the majority carriers → p-type. [1]

items.q: An electron is released from rest in a uniform electric field of 2×10⁴ N/C between two charged plates. Find (i) its acceleration, (ii) the time it takes to travel 1.5 cm. (e = 1.6×10⁻¹⁹ C, m_e = 9.11×10⁻³¹ kg; neglect gravity)

A straight horizontal wire of mass 20 g and length 0.5 m is placed in a uniform horizontal magnetic field of 0.4 T perpendicular to the wire. What current must flow in it so that it stays suspended in mid-air? How should the direction of current be chosen? (g = 9.8 m/s²)
items.ans:
For suspension the magnetic force balances the weight: BIl = mg → I = mg/(Bl) = (0.02 × 9.8)/(0.4 × 0.5) = 0.98 A. [1]
Direction: chosen so that the force IL × B points vertically upward (by Fleming's left-hand rule), e.g. for B pointing north, current must flow from west to east. [1]

items.q: A ray of light falls normally on one face of an equilateral glass prism of refractive index √2. Find the critical angle for glass and trace the path of the ray. Will it emerge from the second face?
items.ans:
Critical angle: sin C = 1/√2 → C = 45°. [1]
The ray enters undeviated (normal incidence) and meets the second face at an angle of incidence equal to the prism angle, 60°. Since 60° is greater than 45°, it is totally internally reflected and does not emerge from the second face; the reflected ray then meets the third face normally and passes out undeviated. [1]

items.q: The total energy of the electron in the ground state of a hydrogen atom is −13.6 eV. (i) What are its kinetic and potential energies in this state? (ii) What is the total energy of the electron in the n = 4 state?
items.ans:
(i) In Bohr's model K = −E and U = 2E: K = +13.6 eV, U = −27.2 eV. [1]
(ii) E₄ = −13.6/4² = −0.85 eV. [1]

items.q: A silicon diode (forward voltage drop 0.7 V) is connected in series with a 220 Ω resistor across a 5 V battery so that it is forward biased. Find the current in the circuit. What will the current be (approximately) if the battery terminals are reversed? Give reason.
items.ans:
Forward bias: I = (5 − 0.7)/220 = 4.3/220 ≈ 0.0195 A ≈ 19.5 mA. [1]
Reversed: the diode is reverse biased and offers very high resistance; only a tiny reverse saturation current (of the order of μA or less) flows, so the current is practically zero. [1]

items.q: (i) Compare electrical conductivity of metals, insulators and semiconductors based on band theory. (ii) Explain why diamond is insulator but tin is conductor though both are Group 14.
items.ans:
Metals: Overlapping/partially filled conduction band → free electrons → high conductivity.
Insulators: Large band gap (>5 eV) → negligible thermal excitation → poor conductivity.
Semiconductors: Moderate band gap (~1 eV) → some carriers at room temp → intermediate conductivity.
Diamond: Very large band gap (~5.4 eV) → insulator. Tin: Metallic bonding, overlapping bands → conductor.

items.q: Internal resistance of a car battery decreases as its temperature rises. Explain: (i) why the car starts more easily on a warm day, (ii) why the headlights dim momentarily when the starter motor is switched on, (iii) why the temperature of a heater element becomes constant after some time.
items.ans:
(i) Warm day: lower internal resistance r → larger current I = E/(R + r) for the starter → engine starts easily. [1]
(ii) The starter draws a very large current, so the drop Ir inside the battery is large and the terminal voltage V = E − Ir falls → headlights get less voltage and dim. [1]
(iii) At steady state, rate of heat production (I²R) = rate of heat loss to surroundings → temperature stays constant. [1]

items.q: Calculate binding energy and binding energy per nucleon for oxygen-16. (m_p=1.00727u, m_n=1.00866u, m_O=15.99493u, 1u=931.5 MeV)
Find critical angle for diamond (μ=2.42). A ray hits a face at 30°. Will it undergo total internal reflection? Also explain why diamond sparkles.
items.ans:
θ_c = sin⁻¹(1/2.42) = sin⁻¹(0.413) ≈ 24.4°.
Incident angle 30° is greater than θ_c → total internal reflection occurs.
Diamond is cut so that light undergoes multiple TIR inside before emerging — this causes its sparkle.

items.q: State Huygens' principle. Use it to derive Snell's law of refraction.
items.ans:
Huygens' Principle: Every point on a wavefront is a source of secondary wavelets; new wavefront is tangent to these wavelets.
Derivation: Let AB hit boundary. A reaches medium 2, point B still in medium 1. In time t: B→C (v₁t), A→E (v₂t). Refracted wavefront CE.
sin i = BC/AC = v₁t/AC; sin r = AE/AC = v₂t/AC.
sin i/sin r = v₁/v₂ = n₂/n₁ → n₁ sin i = n₂ sin r (Snell's Law).

items.q: An ammeter reads up to 750 mA; galvanometer has Ig=100 mA, G=13 Ω. (i) Find shunt resistance. (ii) Why is the frame of a galvanometer made of metal?
items.ans:
(i) S = IgG/(I−Ig) = 100×13/(750−100) = 1300/650 = 2 Ω.
(ii) Metal frame provides electromagnetic damping — eddy currents in frame oppose coil oscillation → quick settling.

items.q: A solenoid: N turns, area A, length l. Find (i) Inductance L. If N→5N, A→25A, l→5l, find new inductance.

Using Gauss's law, obtain an expression for the electric field due to an infinitely long straight wire with uniform linear charge density λ. Hence find the field at a distance of 2 cm from a long wire with λ = 3 μC/m.
items.ans:
Take a coaxial cylindrical Gaussian surface of radius r and length l. By symmetry E is radial and has the same magnitude on the curved surface; flux through the flat ends is zero. [1]
Φ = E(2πrl) = q_enc/ε₀ = λl/ε₀ → E = λ/(2πε₀r), directed radially outward for λ positive. [1]
E = 2kλ/r = (2 × 9×10⁹ × 3×10⁻⁶)/0.02 = 2.7×10⁶ N/C. [1]

items.q: When a cell is connected across a 4 Ω resistor the current is 0.5 A; when connected across a 9 Ω resistor the current is 0.25 A. Find (i) the emf and (ii) the internal resistance of the cell. (iii) What is the maximum current the cell can supply?

A metal rod PQ of length 0.5 m slides at a constant speed of 4 m/s on two parallel conducting rails, perpendicular to a uniform magnetic field of 0.2 T. The total resistance of the circuit is 2 Ω. Find (i) the induced emf, (ii) the induced current, (iii) the force required to keep the rod moving at constant speed and the power delivered.
items.ans:
(i) e = Blv = 0.2 × 0.5 × 4 = 0.4 V. [1]
(ii) I = e/R = 0.4/2 = 0.2 A. [1]
(iii) Magnetic force opposing motion F = BIl = 0.2 × 0.2 × 0.5 = 0.02 N, so an equal external force 0.02 N is needed. Power = Fv = 0.02 × 4 = 0.08 W (= I²R = 0.04 × 2). [1]

items.q: A series LCR circuit has L = 0.4 H, C = 25 μF and R = 40 Ω and is connected to a 200 V (rms) source of variable frequency. Find (i) the resonant angular frequency, (ii) the rms current at resonance, (iii) the quality factor of the circuit.

A ray of light passes through an equilateral glass prism such that the angle of minimum deviation is 30°. Find (i) the refractive index of the glass, (ii) the angle of incidence. (iii) How does the ray travel inside the prism in this position?
items.ans:
(i) μ = sin[(A + δ_m)/2]/sin(A/2) = sin 45°/sin 30° = 0.707/0.5 ≈ 1.414 (= √2). [1]
(ii) At minimum deviation i = e = (A + δ_m)/2 = (60° + 30°)/2 = 45°. [1]
(iii) The refracted ray inside travels parallel to the base of the prism (r₁ = r₂ = A/2 = 30°). [1]

items.q: In a hydrogen atom the energy of the electron in the nth orbit is E_n = −13.6/n² eV. (i) Find the wavelength of the photon emitted in the transition n = 3 → n = 2. (ii) Name the spectral series and region it belongs to. (iii) Find the ratio of radii of the 3rd and 2nd orbits.
items.ans:
(i) ΔE = 13.6(1/4 − 1/9) = 13.6 × 5/36 ≈ 1.89 eV. λ = hc/ΔE = 1240 eV nm/1.89 eV ≈ 656 nm. [1]
(ii) Balmer series (final level n = 2); visible region (red line, Hα). [1]
(iii) r ∝ n² → r₃ : r₂ = 9 : 4. [1]

items.q: Calculate the energy released in the fusion reaction ²H + ³H → ⁴He + n. Masses: ²H = 2.014102 u, ³H = 3.016049 u, ⁴He = 4.002603 u, n = 1.008665 u (1 u = 931.5 MeV/c²). Why does such a reaction need a temperature of about 10⁷ K?
items.ans:
Mass of reactants = 2.014102 + 3.016049 = 5.030151 u; products = 4.002603 + 1.008665 = 5.011268 u. [1]
Δm = 0.018883 u → Q = 0.018883 × 931.5 ≈ 17.6 MeV released. [1]
Both nuclei are positively charged; they must have very large kinetic energy to overcome the Coulomb repulsion and come within range of the short-range nuclear force — such energies need temperatures ~10⁷ K. [1]

items.q: Charges of +2 μC, +2 μC and −4 μC are placed at the three corners of an equilateral triangle of side 10 cm. Find (i) the electrostatic potential energy of the system, (ii) the work needed to separate the charges to infinity, (iii) the potential at the centroid of the triangle.
items.ans:
(i) U = k(q₁q₂ + q₂q₃ + q₃q₁)/a = 9×10⁹ × (4 − 8 − 8)×10⁻¹²/0.1 = −1.08 J. [1]
(ii) Work needed = 0 − U = +1.08 J. [1]
(iii) All charges are at the same distance r = a/√3 from the centroid: V = k(2 + 2 − 4)×10⁻⁶/r = 0. [1]

items.q: Two cells, E₁ = 6 V (internal resistance 1 Ω) and E₂ = 4 V (internal resistance 2 Ω), are connected in parallel with their positive terminals joined, and this combination is connected across a 4 Ω resistor. Using Kirchhoff's rules, find the current through each cell and through the resistor.
items.ans:
Let V be the potential of the common positive terminal. Junction rule: (6 − V)/1 + (4 − V)/2 = V/4. [1]
24 − 4V + 8 − 2V = V → V = 32/7 ≈ 4.57 V. [1]
I₁ = (6 − 4.57)/1 ≈ 1.43 A (10/7 A, discharging); I₂ = (4 − 4.57)/2 ≈ −0.29 A, i.e. 0.29 A (2/7 A) flows INTO E₂ (it is being charged); I_R = 4.57/4 ≈ 1.14 A (8/7 A). [1]

items.q: A proton moving at 4×10⁵ m/s enters a uniform magnetic field of 0.05 T at an angle of 60° to the field. Describe its path and find (i) the radius of the path, (ii) the pitch. (m_p = 1.67×10⁻²⁷ kg, e = 1.6×10⁻¹⁹ C)
items.ans:
The velocity component along B (v cos 60°) is unaffected, while the perpendicular component (v sin 60°) gives circular motion → the path is a helix. [1]
(i) r = m v sin θ/(eB) = (1.67×10⁻²⁷ × 4×10⁵ × 0.866)/(1.6×10⁻¹⁹ × 0.05) ≈ 7.2×10⁻² m = 7.2 cm. [1]
(ii) T = 2πm/(eB) ≈ 1.31×10⁻⁶ s; pitch = v cos θ × T = 2×10⁵ × 1.31×10⁻⁶ ≈ 0.26 m. [1]

items.q: A long solenoid with 1000 turns per metre carries a current of 2 A. Its core is filled with a material of relative permeability 400. Find (i) the magnetic intensity H, (ii) the magnetic field B in the core, (iii) the magnetisation M of the core.

In Young's double-slit experiment with light of wavelength 480 nm, the fringe width in air is 2.4 mm when the screen is 1.2 m from the slits. (i) Find the slit separation and the angular fringe width. (ii) Find the fringe width if the whole apparatus is immersed in water (μ = 4/3). (iii) What will be seen if one slit is covered?
items.ans:
(i) d = λD/β = (480×10⁻⁹ × 1.2)/(2.4×10⁻³) = 2.4×10⁻⁴ m = 0.24 mm; angular width θ = λ/d = β/D = 2×10⁻³ rad. [1]
(ii) In water λ' = λ/μ, so β' = β/μ = 2.4 × 3/4 = 1.8 mm. [1]
(iii) The interference fringes disappear; only the diffraction pattern of a single slit (broad bright centre with fainter bands) is seen. [1]

items.q: (i) Sketch the variation of binding energy per nucleon with mass number and state its main features. (ii) A nucleus of mass number 240 (BE per nucleon 7.6 MeV) splits into two nuclei of mass number 120 each (BE per nucleon 8.5 MeV). Find the energy released.
items.ans:
(i) BE/A rises steeply for light nuclei, reaches a broad maximum ≈ 8.75 MeV near A ≈ 56 (Fe), and decreases slowly to ≈ 7.6 MeV for A ≈ 240. Nearly constant BE/A for 30 ≤ A ≤ 170 shows the short-range, saturating nature of nuclear force. [1]
Heavy nuclei gain BE/A by splitting (fission); light nuclei by combining (fusion) — energy is released in both. [1]
(ii) Energy released = BE(products) − BE(parent) = 240 × 8.5 − 240 × 7.6 = 240 × 0.9 = 216 MeV. [1]

items.q: When light of wavelength 300 nm falls on a metal surface, the stopping potential is 1.85 V; for light of wavelength 400 nm it is 0.82 V. From these data find (i) Planck's constant, (ii) the work function of the metal. (e = 1.6×10⁻¹⁹ C, c = 3×10⁸ m/s)
items.ans:
Einstein's equation: eV₀ = hc/λ − φ₀. Subtracting for the two wavelengths: e(V₁ − V₂) = hc(1/λ₁ − 1/λ₂). [1]
(i) h = 1.6×10⁻¹⁹ × 1.03/[3×10⁸ × (1/300 − 1/400)×10⁹] = 1.648×10⁻¹⁹/(3×10⁸ × 8.33×10⁵) ≈ 6.6×10⁻³⁴ J s. [1]
(ii) φ₀ = hc/λ₁ − eV₁ = (6.6×10⁻³⁴ × 3×10⁸/3×10⁻⁷) J − 1.85 eV ≈ 4.13 eV − 1.85 eV ≈ 2.28 eV. [1]

items.q: Capacitors of 3 μF and 6 μF are joined in series, and this combination is connected in parallel with a 4 μF capacitor. The arrangement is charged by a 10 V battery. Find (i) the equivalent capacitance, (ii) the charge on each capacitor and the potential difference across the 3 μF capacitor, (iii) the total energy stored.
items.ans:
(i) Series part: 1/C = 1/3 + 1/6 = 1/2 → 2 μF. Equivalent C = 2 + 4 = 6 μF. [1]
(ii) 4 μF: Q = 4 × 10 = 40 μC. Series branch: Q = 2 × 10 = 20 μC on each of the 3 μF and 6 μF. V across 3 μF = 20/3 ≈ 6.67 V (and 3.33 V across 6 μF). [1]
(iii) U = ½CV² = ½ × 6×10⁻⁶ × 10² = 3×10⁻⁴ J = 300 μJ. [1]

items.q: The tungsten filament of a 100 W, 220 V bulb has a resistance of 40 Ω at room temperature (20 °C). The temperature coefficient of resistance of tungsten is 4.5×10⁻³ °C⁻¹ (assume it constant). Find (i) the resistance of the filament when the bulb glows normally, (ii) the temperature of the filament, (iii) explain why bulbs usually fuse at the moment they are switched on.
items.ans:
(i) Hot resistance R = V²/P = 220²/100 = 484 Ω. [1]
(ii) R = R₀[1 + α(T − 20)] → 484 = 40[1 + 4.5×10⁻³(T − 20)] → T − 20 = 11.1/4.5×10⁻³ ≈ 2467 → T ≈ 2487 °C (about 2490 °C). [1]
(iii) When cold, the resistance is only 40 Ω, so the initial current 220/40 = 5.5 A is about 12 times the normal current (0.45 A). This sudden surge heats weak spots in the filament and can snap it. [1]

items.q: A rectangular coil of 20 turns, 8 cm × 5 cm, carries a current of 2 A in a uniform magnetic field of 0.5 T. The plane of the coil makes an angle of 30° with the field. Find (i) the torque on the coil, (ii) the maximum torque possible. (iii) In which orientation is the coil in stable equilibrium?
items.ans:
Area A = 0.08 × 0.05 = 4×10⁻³ m²; the normal to the coil makes 60° with B. [½]
(i) τ = NIAB sin 60° = 20 × 2 × 4×10⁻³ × 0.5 × 0.866 ≈ 6.9×10⁻² N m. [1]
(ii) τ_max = NIAB = 0.08 N m (when the plane of the coil is parallel to B). [½]
(iii) Stable equilibrium when the magnetic moment (normal to the coil) is parallel to B, i.e. the plane of the coil is perpendicular to the field; torque is then zero and potential energy minimum. [1]

items.q: A bulb rated 60 W, 120 V is to be operated from 240 V, 50 Hz mains by connecting a pure inductor in series with it. Find (i) the current through the bulb when it glows normally, (ii) the inductance required. (iii) Why is an inductor preferred to a resistor for this purpose?
items.ans:
(i) R = V²/P = 120²/60 = 240 Ω; I = P/V = 60/120 = 0.5 A. [1]
(ii) Z = 240/0.5 = 480 Ω; X_L = √(Z² − R²) = √(480² − 240²) ≈ 415.7 Ω; L = X_L/(2πf) = 415.7/(2π × 50) ≈ 1.32 H. [1]
(iii) A pure inductor consumes no average power (current and voltage across it differ in phase by 90°), whereas a series resistor would waste 0.5 × 120 = 60 W as heat. [1]

items.q: An object and a screen are fixed 90 cm apart. A convex lens placed between them gives a sharp image on the screen for two positions of the lens that are 30 cm apart. Find (i) the object distances for the two positions, (ii) the focal length of the lens, (iii) the ratio of the sizes of the two images.
items.ans:
(i) By symmetry the two positions interchange u and v: |u| + |v| = 90 and |v| − |u| = 30 → |u| = 30 cm, |v| = 60 cm for one position, and |u| = 60 cm, |v| = 30 cm for the other. [1]
(ii) 1/f = 1/v − 1/u = 1/60 + 1/30 = 1/20 → f = 20 cm [or f = (D² − d²)/4D = (8100 − 900)/360 = 20 cm]. [1]
(iii) Magnifications are 60/30 = 2 and 30/60 = 0.5, so the image sizes are in the ratio 4 : 1 (both real, inverted). [1]

items.q: In a Geiger–Marsden experiment, an α-particle of kinetic energy 5.0 MeV moves head-on towards a gold nucleus (Z = 79). (i) Find its distance of closest approach. (ii) What is the impact parameter and the scattering angle in this case? (iii) What does this distance tell us about the size of the nucleus?
items.ans:
(i) At closest approach K = k(2e)(Ze)/r₀ → r₀ = (9×10⁹ × 2 × 79 × (1.6×10⁻¹⁹)²)/(5 × 1.6×10⁻¹³) ≈ 4.6×10⁻¹⁴ m (≈ 46 fm). [1]
(ii) Head-on: impact parameter b = 0; the α-particle retraces its path, scattering angle 180°. [1]
(iii) The nucleus must be smaller than about 4.6×10⁻¹⁴ m — this gives an upper limit to nuclear size, about 10⁻⁴ of the atomic size (10⁻¹⁰ m). [1]

items.q: A laser pointer emits 5 mW of light of wavelength 663 nm. Find (i) the energy of each photon in eV, (ii) the number of photons emitted per second. (iii) Will this light eject photoelectrons from caesium (work function 2.14 eV)? Would a more powerful laser of the same wavelength help? (h = 6.63×10⁻³⁴ J s)
items.ans:
(i) E = hc/λ = (6.63×10⁻³⁴ × 3×10⁸)/(663×10⁻⁹) = 3.0×10⁻¹⁹ J ≈ 1.88 eV. [1]
(ii) N = P/E = 5×10⁻³/3.0×10⁻¹⁹ ≈ 1.7×10¹⁶ photons per second. [1]
(iii) No — 1.88 eV is less than 2.14 eV. A more powerful laser only gives more photons of the same energy, and each electron absorbs one photon, so still no emission. [1]

items.q: (i) Using Gauss's law, obtain the electric field due to an infinite plane sheet with uniform surface charge density σ. (ii) Two large, thin parallel metal plates carry surface charge densities +17.7 nC/m² and −17.7 nC/m² on their inner faces. Find the electric field in the region between them and outside them. (ε₀ = 8.85×10⁻¹² C² N⁻¹ m⁻²)
items.ans:
(i) Take a cylindrical Gaussian surface of cross-section A piercing the sheet; E is perpendicular to the sheet, so flux passes only through the two flat ends: Φ = 2EA. Enclosed charge = σA. 2EA = σA/ε₀ → E = σ/(2ε₀), directed away from the sheet for σ positive. [1½]
(ii) Between the plates the fields of the two sheets add: E = σ/ε₀ = 17.7×10⁻⁹/8.85×10⁻¹² = 2×10³ N/C, from the positive to the negative plate. [1]
Outside, the two fields are equal and opposite → E = 0. [½]

items.q: Six identical cells, each of emf 1.5 V and internal resistance 0.5 Ω, are connected in series to an external resistance of 6 Ω. Find (i) the current in the circuit, (ii) the potential difference across the external resistance. (iii) Find the current if one of the cells is connected the wrong way round by mistake.
items.ans:
(i) Total emf = 6 × 1.5 = 9 V; total internal resistance = 6 × 0.5 = 3 Ω. I = 9/(6 + 3) = 1 A. [1]
(ii) V = IR = 1 × 6 = 6 V. [1]
(iii) The reversed cell opposes: net emf = 5 × 1.5 − 1.5 = 6 V, but internal resistance is still 3 Ω. I = 6/9 ≈ 0.67 A. [1]

items.q: A wire carrying a current of 4 A is bent into a semicircular arc of radius 5 cm. The current is led in and out of the arc by two long straight wires that lie along the radial lines through the two ends of the arc (extending outward, away from the centre). Find the magnetic field at the centre of the arc. Why do the straight portions contribute nothing? State the direction of the field.
items.ans:
Biot–Savart: each element of the arc is perpendicular to the line joining it to the centre, so B_arc = (μ₀I/4πR) × πR/R = μ₀I/(4R). [1]
B = (4π×10⁻⁷ × 4)/(4 × 0.05) ≈ 2.5×10⁻⁵ T. [1]
The straight parts lie along lines through the centre, so dl × r = 0 for them and they contribute no field. Direction: perpendicular to the plane of the arc, given by the right-hand rule (out of the page for anticlockwise current as seen by the viewer). [1]

items.q: A step-down transformer at a village substation is not 100% efficient. Name three causes of energy loss in a real transformer and state how each is reduced in practice.
items.ans:
(1) Copper (joule) loss: heating I²R in the windings — reduced by using thick copper wire for the high-current winding. [1]
(2) Eddy-current loss: currents induced in the iron core heat it — reduced by using a laminated core (thin insulated sheets). [1]
(3) Flux leakage: not all primary flux links the secondary — reduced by winding the primary and secondary one over the other on a closed (shell-type) core. (Also acceptable: hysteresis loss in the core, reduced by using soft iron with a narrow loop; humming/vibration losses.) [1]

items.q: In a Young's double-slit experiment, the slits are 0.3 mm apart and the screen is 1.2 m away. The slits are illuminated by light containing two wavelengths, 600 nm and 480 nm. Find (i) the distance of the third bright fringe of the 600 nm light from the central maximum, (ii) the least distance from the central maximum at which bright fringes of both wavelengths coincide, (iii) the ratio of the fringe widths of the two patterns.

When lithium-7 is bombarded with protons, the reaction ⁷₃Li + ¹₁H → ⁴₂He + ⁴₂He takes place. (i) Show that charge and the number of nucleons are conserved. (ii) Find the energy released (Q-value). (iii) In what form does this energy mainly appear? Masses: ⁷Li = 7.016004 u, ¹H = 1.007825 u, ⁴He = 4.002603 u; 1 u = 931.5 MeV/c².
items.ans:
(i) Charge: 3 + 1 = 2 + 2 = 4; nucleons: 7 + 1 = 4 + 4 = 8 — both conserved. [1]
(ii) Δm = (7.016004 + 1.007825) − 2 × 4.002603 = 8.023829 − 8.005206 = 0.018623 u; Q = 0.018623 × 931.5 ≈ 17.3 MeV. [1]
(iii) Mainly as kinetic energy of the two α-particles, which fly apart (the energy comes from the increase in total binding energy). [1]

items.q: Explain, with a labelled circuit diagram, how a p-n junction diode works as a half-wave rectifier. Draw (describe) the input and output waveforms. Why is a full-wave rectifier usually preferred, and what is the output frequency of each for a 50 Hz input?
items.ans:
Circuit: AC from the secondary of a transformer is applied to a diode in series with a load resistor R_L; output taken across R_L. [1]
During the positive half-cycle the diode is forward biased and conducts, so current flows through R_L; during the negative half-cycle it is reverse biased and practically no current flows. Output: positive half-sine pulses with gaps (pulsating DC). [1]
A full-wave rectifier uses both half-cycles, giving higher average output and easier smoothing. Output (ripple) frequency: half-wave 50 Hz, full-wave 100 Hz. [1]

items.q:
[CBQ] Doping Silicon at a Chip Fab
A semiconductor fab coming up at Dholera, Gujarat, receives extremely pure silicon wafers. Engineers add tiny, controlled amounts of impurity atoms (about 1 impurity atom per 10⁷ silicon atoms) to create n-type and p-type regions.
(i) Name one impurity used to make n-type silicon and state its valency. [1m]
(ii) Why does a doped wafer conduct far better than pure silicon at room temperature, though the impurity is only 1 part in 10⁷? [1m]
(iii) In p-type silicon, which charge carriers are in majority? Is the crystal as a whole charged? [1m]
(iv) Where does the donor energy level lie in the energy band diagram of n-type silicon? [1m]
items.ans:
(i) Phosphorus (or arsenic/antimony) — pentavalent (valency 5).
(ii) Each donor atom easily gives one free electron at room temperature; 1 in 10⁷ of ~5×10²⁸ Si atoms/m³ gives ~5×10²¹ electrons/m³, far more than the intrinsic carrier density (~10¹⁶ m⁻³).
(iii) Holes are majority carriers. The crystal is electrically neutral overall (charge of holes is balanced by the fixed negative acceptor ions).
(iv) Just below the bottom of the conduction band (about 0.01–0.05 eV below it), inside the band gap.

items.q:
[CBQ] Photoelectric Effect Investigation
A lab uses UV light on sodium surface (work function φ₀ = 2 eV). Experiment varies frequency and intensity.
(i) Define work function. [1m]
(ii) Explain why increasing intensity increases photocurrent but not KE. [1m]
(iii) Light of frequency 1.2×10¹⁵ Hz hits the surface. Find maximum KE. [1m]
(iv) State two observations of the photoelectric effect that CANNOT be explained by the wave theory of light. [1m]
items.ans:
(i) Work function: minimum energy required to remove an electron from the metal surface.
(ii) More intensity = more photons per second → more electrons emitted → more current. But each photon's energy hν depends only on frequency, so KE_max is unchanged.
(iii) E = hν = 6.63×10⁻³⁴ × 1.2×10¹⁵ J ≈ 4.96 eV. KE_max = E − φ₀ ≈ 4.96 − 2 ≈ 2.96 eV (≈ 3 eV).
(iv) (a) KE_max depends on frequency, not on intensity; (b) emission is instantaneous, with no time lag even for very dim light (also: existence of a threshold frequency).

items.q:
[CBQ] Optical Fibres for Village Internet
Under the BharatNet project, optical fibre cables carry internet to gram panchayats. Each fibre has a glass core of refractive index 1.50 surrounded by a cladding of refractive index 1.45. Light signals travel kilometres through the core with very little loss.
(i) Name the phenomenon that keeps light inside the core. [1m]
(ii) Why must the cladding have a lower refractive index than the core? [1m]
(iii) Find the critical angle at the core–cladding interface. [1m]
(iv) A ray inside the core strikes the core–cladding interface at an angle of incidence of 70°. Will it be guided along the fibre? Give reason. [1m]
items.ans:
(i) Total internal reflection.
(ii) TIR is possible only when light goes from a denser to a rarer medium, so the cladding must be optically rarer (lower μ) than the core.
(iii) sin C = μ_cladding/μ_core = 1.45/1.50 ≈ 0.967 → C ≈ 75.2°.
(iv) No. 70° is less than the critical angle 75.2°, so the ray is partly refracted into the cladding and the signal leaks out instead of being totally reflected.

items.q:
[CBQ] Inside a Phone Charger
A student in a hostel opens an old mobile charger. It has a small step-down transformer, two diodes connected as a centre-tap full-wave rectifier, and a capacitor across the output. The mains supply is 230 V, 50 Hz.
(i) What property of a p-n junction diode makes it useful for rectification? [1m]
(ii) What is the frequency of the ripple in the rectified output? [1m]
(iii) How many diodes conduct during each half-cycle of the input? [1m]
(iv) What is the role of the capacitor connected across the output? [1m]
items.ans:
(i) It conducts (low resistance) only in forward bias and offers very high resistance in reverse bias — current flows in one direction only.
(ii) Full-wave rectifier: ripple frequency = 2 × 50 = 100 Hz.
(iii) One diode conducts in each half-cycle (the two diodes conduct alternately), so current through the load is always in the same direction.
(iv) It acts as a filter: it charges near the peak and discharges slowly through the load, smoothing the pulsating DC into nearly steady DC.

items.q:
[CBQ] Spectacles for the Back Bench
Riya, a Class XII student in Pune, cannot read the board clearly from the last bench. An optometrist prescribes spectacles of power −0.5 D. Her grandfather uses reading glasses of power +2.5 D.
(i) What is the nature and focal length of Riya's lens? [1m]
(ii) Where does her lens form the image of a very distant object? [1m]
(iii) Riya looks through her lens at a notice board 6 m away. Find the position of the image. [1m]
(iv) If Riya's lens and her grandfather's lens are held in contact, what is the power of the combination? [1m]
items.ans:
(i) Diverging (concave) lens; f = 1/P = 1/(−0.5) m = −2 m (−200 cm).
(ii) At its focus — a virtual, erect, diminished image 2 m in front of the lens (same side as the object).
(iii) 1/v − 1/u = 1/f → 1/v = 1/(−2) + 1/(−6) = −2/3 → v = −1.5 m: virtual image 1.5 m in front of the lens.
(iv) P = P₁ + P₂ = −0.5 + 2.5 = +2.0 D (converging, f = 50 cm).

items.q:
[CBQ] Diode Characteristics in the School Lab
Students in a Lucknow school lab record the forward characteristic of a silicon diode. The current is almost zero up to about 0.6 V and then rises sharply: at 0.70 V it is 10 mA and at 0.75 V it is 30 mA.
(i) What is the threshold (knee) voltage, and why is the current nearly zero below it? [1m]
(ii) Find the dynamic resistance of the diode between 0.70 V and 0.75 V. [1m]
(iii) How does the width of the depletion layer change when the forward voltage is increased? [1m]
(iv) Why is the diode called a non-ohmic device? [1m]
items.ans:
(i) About 0.7 V for silicon. Below it the applied voltage cannot overcome the barrier potential, so very few majority carriers cross the junction.
(ii) r_d = ΔV/ΔI = (0.75 − 0.70)/(30 − 10)×10⁻³ = 0.05/0.020 = 2.5 Ω.
(iii) It decreases — the forward voltage opposes the barrier potential, so the depletion layer becomes narrower.
(iv) Its V–I graph is not a straight line (current does not vary linearly with voltage) and it conducts differently in forward and reverse bias, so Ohm's law is not obeyed.

items.q:
[CBQ] Prism Periscope in an Army Bunker
Soldiers at a border post in Ladakh observe the area from inside a bunker using a periscope. Instead of plane mirrors, it uses two right-angled isosceles glass prisms (refractive index 1.5). Light enters one face normally and meets the hypotenuse face at an angle of incidence of 45°.
(i) Name the phenomenon that turns the light through 90° in each prism. [1m]
(ii) Find the critical angle for the glass–air surface. [1m]
(iii) Would the periscope still work if the prisms were made of a material of refractive index 1.3? Give reason. [1m]
(iv) Give one advantage of using such prisms in place of plane mirrors. [1m]
items.ans:
(i) Total internal reflection at the hypotenuse face.
(ii) sin C = 1/μ = 1/1.5 = 0.667 → C ≈ 41.8°.
(iii) No. For μ = 1.3, C = sin⁻¹(1/1.3) ≈ 50.3°; the angle of incidence 45° is less than C, so the light would be partly refracted out instead of being totally reflected.
(iv) TIR reflects almost 100% of the light (brighter image), and there is no silvering to tarnish or peel off; no multiple images as in a thick glass mirror.

items.q:
[CBQ] Temperature Sensor in a Baby Incubator
A primary health centre in Odisha uses baby incubators whose temperature is controlled by a sensor made of a semiconductor. As the semiconductor warms up, its resistance falls noticeably, and the control circuit switches the heater off. The band gap of the material is about 1.1 eV.
(i) Why does the resistance of a semiconductor fall when its temperature rises? [1m]
(ii) In a pure (intrinsic) semiconductor, how does the number of free electrons compare with the number of holes? [1m]
(iii) Can a photon of wavelength 600 nm create an electron–hole pair in this material? Show by calculation. [1m]
(iv) Find the longest wavelength of light that can create an electron–hole pair in this material. [1m]
items.ans:
(i) More electrons gain enough thermal energy to cross the band gap into the conduction band, creating more electron–hole pairs; the increase in carriers far outweighs the small fall in mobility, so resistance falls.
(ii) They are equal (n_e = n_h = n_i), since each electron that crosses the gap leaves one hole behind.
(iii) E = hc/λ ≈ 1240/600 ≈ 2.07 eV, which is more than 1.1 eV, so yes, it can.
(iv) λ_max = hc/E_g ≈ 1240/1.1 ≈ 1130 nm (≈ 1.13 μm, in the infrared).

items.q:
[CBQ] Fuel for a Nuclear Power Station
The Kudankulam power station in Tamil Nadu produces electricity from the fission of uranium-235. A typical fission is ²³⁵U + n → ¹⁴¹Ba + ⁹²Kr + 3n, and each fission releases about 200 MeV. Consider a reactor that produces 3000 MW of heat. (1 MeV = 1.6×10⁻¹³ J, Avogadro number = 6.022×10²³ mol⁻¹)
(i) Why is energy released when a heavy nucleus splits into two medium-mass nuclei? [1m]
(ii) How many fissions take place every second in this reactor? [1m]
(iii) Estimate the mass of U-235 used up in one day. [1m]
(iv) How much mass is converted into energy in one day? [1m]
items.ans:
(i) The fission fragments have a higher binding energy per nucleon (≈ 8.5 MeV) than U-235 (≈ 7.6 MeV); the increase in total binding energy is released (mass defect → energy).
(ii) Energy per fission = 200 × 1.6×10⁻¹³ = 3.2×10⁻¹¹ J. Fissions per second = 3×10⁹/3.2×10⁻¹¹ ≈ 9.4×10¹⁹ s⁻¹.
(iii) Per day: 9.375×10¹⁹ × 86400 ≈ 8.1×10²⁴ nuclei; mass = (8.1×10²⁴/6.022×10²³) × 235 g ≈ 3.2×10³ g ≈ 3.2 kg.
(iv) Energy per day = 3×10⁹ × 86400 ≈ 2.6×10¹⁴ J; Δm = E/c² = 2.6×10¹⁴/(9×10¹⁶) ≈ 2.9×10⁻³ kg ≈ 2.9 g.

items.q:
[CBQ] The Jeweller's Magnifier
A goldsmith in Jaipur checks the hallmark on a gold ring using a small magnifying glass (a convex lens of focal length 5 cm) held close to his eye. His near point is 25 cm.
(i) Find the magnifying power when the final image is formed at his near point. [1m]
(ii) Find the magnifying power when the image is at infinity (relaxed eye). [1m]
(iii) How far from the lens should the ring be held so that the image forms at 25 cm? [1m]
(iv) Why would a lens of focal length 2.5 cm suit him better for very fine engraving? [1m]
items.ans:
(i) m = 1 + D/f = 1 + 25/5 = 6.
(ii) m = D/f = 25/5 = 5.
(iii) v = −25 cm, f = +5 cm: 1/u = 1/v − 1/f = −1/25 − 1/5 = −6/25 → u ≈ −4.17 cm, i.e. about 4.2 cm in front of the lens (just inside the focus).
(iv) Magnifying power ∝ 1/f: with f = 2.5 cm, m = 1 + 25/2.5 = 11 (or 10 at infinity), so finer details look larger.

items.q:
(A) A parallel plate capacitor has plates of area A separated by d, with dielectric K between them.
(i) An isolated conductor always has small capacitance — why? [2m]
(ii) Three capacitors 6μF, 9μF, 18μF: find minimum and maximum capacitance. [2m]
(iii) Two other factors (besides area) on which capacitance depends. [1m]
items.ans:
(i) C = 4πε₀R for isolated sphere → depends only on radius. Very large capacitance needs impractically large sphere.
(ii) Min (series): 1/C = 1/6+1/9+1/18 = 6/18 → C_min = 3 μF.
    Max (parallel): C_max = 6+9+18 = 33 μF.
(iii) Distance between plates (C ∝ 1/d), dielectric constant of the medium between the plates (C ∝ K).
items.orq:
(B) Two long parallel wires carry currents I₁ and I₂ separated by distance d.
(i) Derive expression for force per unit length between them. [3m]
(ii) State condition for attraction/repulsion. [1m]
(iii) Define 1 Ampere using this force law. [1m]
items.orans:
(i) B₁ = μ₀I₁/2πd. Force on length L of wire 2: F = I₂LB₁ = μ₀I₁I₂L/2πd. Per unit length: F/L = μ₀I₁I₂/2πd.
(ii) Same direction currents → attract; opposite directions → repel.
(iii) 1 A is that current which, when flowing in each of two infinitely long parallel wires 1 m apart in vacuum, produces force of 2×10⁻⁷ N per metre length.

items.q:
(A) Explain Young's Double Slit Experiment:
(i) Derive expression for fringe width β. [3m]
(ii) What happens to fringe width if: (a) slit separation halved (b) screen distance doubled. [2m]
items.ans:
(i) Path difference = dy/D (d=slit sep, y=position, D=screen dist). For bright: dy/D = nλ → y_n = nλD/d. Fringe width β = λD/d.
(ii) (a) d→d/2 → β doubles. (b) D→2D → β doubles.
items.orq:
(B) (i) Distinguish between nuclear fission and fusion with one example each. [2m]
(ii) In fission of U-235, about 0.1% mass converts to energy. Energy from 1 kg? [3m]
items.orans:
(i) Fission: heavy nucleus splits → lighter nuclei + energy. E.g., U-235 + n → Ba-141 + Kr-92 + 3n.
Fusion: light nuclei combine → heavier nucleus + energy. E.g., ²H+³H → ⁴He + n.
(ii) E = mc² = 0.001×1×(3×10⁸)² = 9×10¹³ J.

items.q:
(A) (i) Derive the lens maker's formula 1/f = (μ − 1)(1/R₁ − 1/R₂) for a thin double-convex lens. [3m]
(ii) A double-convex lens of glass (μ = 1.5) has radii of curvature 20 cm and 30 cm. Find its focal length and power in air. [2m]
items.ans:
(i) Refraction at first surface (object O in air, image I₁): μ/v₁ − 1/u = (μ − 1)/R₁.
I₁ acts as object for second surface (glass to air): 1/v − μ/v₁ = (1 − μ)/R₂.
Adding: 1/v − 1/u = (μ − 1)(1/R₁ − 1/R₂). For u = ∞, v = f → 1/f = (μ − 1)(1/R₁ − 1/R₂). [3]
(ii) R₁ = +20 cm, R₂ = −30 cm: 1/f = 0.5(1/20 + 1/30) = 0.5 × 1/12 = 1/24 → f = 24 cm. [1]
P = 100/f(cm) = 100/24 ≈ +4.17 D. [1]
items.orq:
(B) (i) State and prove Ampere's circuital law. [3m]
(ii) A solenoid 1m long, 1000 turns carries 2A. Find B inside. [2m]
items.orans:
(i) Ampere's Law: ∮B·dl = μ₀I_enclosed. For a closed loop, circulation of B = μ₀ × current enclosed.
Proof for infinite wire: By symmetry B is tangential, constant on circular path of radius r. B×2πr = μ₀I → B = μ₀I/2πr.
(ii) B = μ₀nI = μ₀(N/L)I = 4π×10⁻⁷ × 1000 × 2 = 8π×10⁻⁴ T ≈ 2.51×10⁻³ T.

items.q:
(A) (i) Derive an expression for the capacitance of a parallel plate capacitor (plate area A, separation d) when a dielectric slab of dielectric constant K and thickness t (t less than d) is placed between the plates. [3m]
(ii) A capacitor has plate area 0.02 m² and separation 4 mm. A slab of thickness 2 mm and K = 4 is inserted. Find its capacitance. [2m]
items.ans:
(i) Field in air gaps E₀ = σ/ε₀; inside slab E = E₀/K. Potential difference V = E₀(d − t) + (E₀/K)t = (σ/ε₀)(d − t + t/K). [2]
C = Q/V = σA/V = ε₀A/(d − t + t/K). [1]
(ii) C = (8.85×10⁻¹² × 0.02)/(0.004 − 0.002 + 0.002/4) = 1.77×10⁻¹³/0.0025 ≈ 7.08×10⁻¹¹ F ≈ 70.8 pF. [2]
items.orq:
(B) (i) Derive an expression for the electric field at a point on the axial line of an electric dipole and show that for r much greater than a, E = 2kp/r³. [3m]
(ii) Charges ±5 nC are 2 mm apart. Find the electric field at 10 cm from the centre of the dipole (a) on its axis, (b) on its equatorial line. [2m]
items.orans:
(i) Charges −q at A and +q at B, separation 2a; point P on axis at distance r from centre. E₊ = kq/(r − a)², E₋ = kq/(r + a)² (opposite). [1]
E = kq[1/(r − a)² − 1/(r + a)²] = kq·4ar/(r² − a²)² = 2kpr/(r² − a²)², along p (p = 2aq). [1]
For r ≫ a: E = 2kp/r³. [1]
(ii) p = 5×10⁻⁹ × 2×10⁻³ = 10⁻¹¹ C m. (a) E_axial = 2kp/r³ = 2 × 9×10⁹ × 10⁻¹¹/(0.1)³ = 180 N/C. [1]
(b) E_equatorial = kp/r³ = 90 N/C, directed opposite to p. [1]

items.q:
(A) (i) State the principle of a transformer and, for an ideal transformer, derive V_s/V_p = N_s/N_p. [3m]
(ii) A transformer steps 220 V mains down to 11 V for a set of LED lamps in a shop. The primary has 2200 turns. Find the number of secondary turns. If the secondary current is 4 A and the efficiency is 90%, find the primary current. [2m]
items.ans:
(i) Principle: mutual induction — an alternating current in the primary produces a changing flux in the core that induces an emf in the secondary. [1]
Same flux φ links each turn: ε_p = −N_p dφ/dt, ε_s = −N_s dφ/dt. [1]
For ideal transformer (no losses, negligible resistance) V_p ≈ ε_p, V_s ≈ ε_s → V_s/V_p = N_s/N_p. [1]
(ii) N_s = 2200 × 11/220 = 110 turns. [1]
P_out = 11 × 4 = 44 W; P_in = 44/0.9 ≈ 48.9 W → I_p = 48.9/220 ≈ 0.22 A. [1]
items.orq:
(B) (i) Using the Biot–Savart law, derive an expression for the magnetic field on the axis of a circular current loop of radius R at a distance x from its centre. [3m]
(ii) A coil of 50 turns and radius 10 cm carries 2 A. Find the magnetic field at its centre and at a point on its axis 10 cm from the centre. [2m]
items.orans:
(i) Element dl at the loop; distance to P is r = √(R² + x²), dl ⊥ r. dB = μ₀I dl/(4πr²). [1]
Components perpendicular to the axis cancel in pairs; axial components add: dB_x = dB·R/r. [1]
B = (μ₀IR/(4πr³))·2πR = μ₀IR²/[2(R² + x²)^(3/2)], along the axis. [1]
(ii) Centre: B = μ₀NI/(2R) = (4π×10⁻⁷ × 50 × 2)/(0.2) ≈ 6.28×10⁻⁴ T. [1]
At x = R: B = B_centre/(2)^(3/2) ≈ 6.28×10⁻⁴/2.83 ≈ 2.22×10⁻⁴ T. [1]

items.q:
(A) (i) Draw a labelled ray diagram of an astronomical refracting telescope in normal adjustment and derive an expression for its magnifying power. [3m]
(ii) A telescope has an objective of focal length 150 cm and an eyepiece of focal length 5 cm. Find its magnifying power and length in normal adjustment. Why is the objective made of large aperture? [2m]
items.ans:
(i) Ray diagram: parallel rays from a distant object pass through the objective (large f₀) and form a real, inverted image at its focus, which is also the focus of the eyepiece; rays emerge parallel, final image at infinity. [1]
Object subtends α at objective; final image subtends β at eye. tan α ≈ α = h/f₀, tan β ≈ β = h/f_e (h = size of intermediate image). [1]
m = β/α = f₀/f_e. [1]
(ii) m = 150/5 = 30; length L = f₀ + f_e = 155 cm. [1]
Large aperture gathers more light (brighter image) and gives better resolution of distant objects. [1]
items.orq:
(B) (i) Explain the formation of the diffraction pattern due to a single slit illuminated by monochromatic light and show that the angular width of the central maximum is 2λ/a. [3m]
(ii) Light of wavelength 500 nm falls on a slit of width 0.2 mm; the screen is 2 m away. Find the linear width of the central maximum. What happens to this width if the slit width is doubled? [2m]
items.orans:
(i) Each point of the slit acts as a source of secondary wavelets (Huygens). At θ = 0 all wavelets are in phase → bright central maximum. [1]
Divide the slit into two halves: at a sin θ = λ each point of the upper half has a partner in the lower half with path difference λ/2 → cancellation → first minimum. Minima at a sin θ = nλ; secondary maxima (fainter) roughly at a sin θ = (n + ½)λ. [1]
Central maximum lies between θ = ±λ/a → angular width = 2λ/a. [1]
(ii) Linear width = 2λD/a = (2 × 500×10⁻⁹ × 2)/(0.2×10⁻³) = 0.01 m = 10 mm. [1]
If a is doubled, the width is halved (5 mm) — the pattern becomes narrower. [1]

items.q:
(A) (i) Obtain the relation I = neAv_d between current and drift velocity of free electrons in a conductor. Hence show that resistivity ρ = m/(ne²τ). [3m]
(ii) A copper wire of cross-section 1.0 mm² carries a current of 1.5 A. The free-electron density of copper is 8.5×10²⁸ m⁻³. Find the drift velocity. Why does a bulb glow almost instantly even though this speed is so small? [2m]
items.ans:
(i) In time Δt, electrons within length v_dΔt cross a section: charge = neA v_dΔt. I = q/Δt = neAv_d. [1]
v_d = eEτ/m and E = V/l → I = neA(eVτ/(ml)) → V/I = R = ml/(ne²τA). [1]
Comparing with R = ρl/A: ρ = m/(ne²τ). [1]
(ii) v_d = I/(neA) = 1.5/(8.5×10²⁸ × 1.6×10⁻¹⁹ × 10⁻⁶) ≈ 1.1×10⁻⁴ m/s (≈ 0.11 mm/s). [1]
The electric field is set up along the whole circuit almost at the speed of light, so free electrons everywhere start drifting at once. [1]
items.orq:
(B) (i) Using Gauss's law, find the electric field due to a uniformly charged thin spherical shell of radius R at (a) a point outside, (b) a point inside the shell. [3m]
(ii) A thin spherical shell of radius 10 cm carries a charge of 4 nC. Find the electric field at 5 cm and at 20 cm from its centre, and the surface charge density. [2m]
items.orans:
(i) (a) Outside (r greater than R): concentric Gaussian sphere of radius r; by symmetry E is radial and uniform on it. E·4πr² = q/ε₀ → E = q/(4πε₀r²), as if the whole charge were at the centre. [2]
(b) Inside (r less than R): Gaussian sphere encloses no charge → E·4πr² = 0 → E = 0. [1]
(ii) At 5 cm (inside): E = 0. At 20 cm: E = kq/r² = 9×10⁹ × 4×10⁻⁹/(0.2)² = 900 N/C, radially outward. [1]
σ = q/(4πR²) = 4×10⁻⁹/(4π × 0.01) ≈ 3.18×10⁻⁸ C/m². [1]

items.q:
(A) (i) Using a phasor diagram, derive expressions for the impedance of a series LCR circuit and the phase angle between voltage and current. [3m]
(ii) A series circuit has R = 60 Ω, X_L = 120 Ω and X_C = 40 Ω, connected to a 220 V (rms) AC supply. Find the impedance, rms current and average power consumed. [2m]
items.ans:
(i) Current I is common. V_R in phase with I, V_L leads I by 90°, V_C lags I by 90°. [1]
Resultant V = √[V_R² + (V_L − V_C)²] = I√[R² + (X_L − X_C)²] → Z = √[R² + (X_L − X_C)²]. [1]
tan φ = (X_L − X_C)/R; voltage leads current if X_L is greater than X_C. [1]
(ii) Z = √[60² + (120 − 40)²] = √(3600 + 6400) = 100 Ω; I_rms = 220/100 = 2.2 A. [1]
cos φ = R/Z = 0.6; P = V_rms I_rms cos φ = 220 × 2.2 × 0.6 ≈ 290 W (= I²R = 4.84 × 60). [1]
items.orq:
(B) (i) Describe the principle of an AC generator and show that the emf induced in its coil is e = NBAω sin ωt. [3m]
(ii) A coil of 100 turns and area 0.05 m² rotates at 50 revolutions per second in a uniform magnetic field of 0.1 T. Find the peak and rms values of the induced emf. [2m]
items.orans:
(i) Principle: electromagnetic induction — when a coil rotates in a magnetic field, the flux linked with it changes and an emf is induced. [1]
At time t the normal to the coil makes angle θ = ωt with B: flux linkage = NBA cos ωt. [1]
e = −d(NBA cos ωt)/dt = NBAω sin ωt; peak e₀ = NBAω. [1]
(ii) ω = 2π × 50 ≈ 314 rad/s; e₀ = 100 × 0.1 × 0.05 × 314 ≈ 157 V. [1]
e_rms = e₀/√2 ≈ 111 V. [1]

items.q:
(A) (i) Draw a ray diagram for a concave mirror forming a real image of an object placed beyond C, and derive the mirror equation 1/v + 1/u = 1/f. [3m]
(ii) The rear-view mirror of a bus is a convex mirror of radius of curvature 40 cm. An object 2 cm tall is placed 30 cm in front of it. Find the position, nature and size of the image. [2m]
items.ans:
(i) Ray parallel to axis reflects through F; ray through C retraces; they meet at the real, inverted image A'B'. Triangles A'B'F and MPF (paraxial, P ≈ M) are similar: A'B'/AB = B'F/FP. Triangles A'B'P and ABP: A'B'/AB = B'P/BP. [1]
So B'F/FP = B'P/BP → (v − f)/f = v/u using sign convention (u, v, f negative). [1]
Rearranging: uv − uf = vf → dividing by uvf: 1/v + 1/u = 1/f. [1]
(ii) f = +20 cm, u = −30 cm: 1/v = 1/20 − 1/(−30) = 1/20 + 1/30 = 1/12 → v = +12 cm (behind the mirror). [1]
m = −v/u = −12/(−30) = +0.4 → image is virtual, erect, diminished, height 0.8 cm. [1]
items.orq:
(B) (i) Draw a ray diagram of a compound microscope forming the final image at the least distance of distinct vision D and derive an expression for its magnifying power. [3m]
(ii) A compound microscope has an objective of focal length 1.25 cm and an eyepiece of focal length 5 cm. An object is placed 1.5 cm from the objective and the final image is formed at 25 cm. Find the magnifying power and the separation of the lenses. [2m]
items.orans:
(i) Objective (short f₀) forms a real, inverted, magnified image A'B' just inside the focus of the eyepiece; the eyepiece acts as a simple magnifier forming the final virtual image at D. [1]
m_o = v_o/u_o (≈ L/f₀ for the image near the eyepiece focus); m_e = 1 + D/f_e. [1]
M = m_o × m_e = (v_o/|u_o|)(1 + D/f_e). [1]
(ii) Objective: 1/v_o = 1/1.25 + 1/(−1.5) = 0.8 − 0.667 = 0.133 → v_o = 7.5 cm; m_o = 7.5/1.5 = 5 (inverted). m_e = 1 + 25/5 = 6 → M = 30. [1]
Eyepiece: 1/u_e = 1/(−25) − 1/5 = −6/25 → u_e = −4.17 cm. Separation = 7.5 + 4.17 ≈ 11.7 cm. [1]

items.q:
(A) (i) Derive an expression for the electric potential at a point at distance r from the centre of a short electric dipole, along a line making angle θ with the dipole axis. Hence show that the potential is zero everywhere on the equatorial line. [3m]
(ii) Charges of +3 nC and −3 nC are 4 mm apart. Find the potential at a point 20 cm from the centre of the dipole on its axis (on the side of the positive charge). How much work is needed to move a small charge along the equatorial line? [2m]
items.ans:
(i) Distances of P from +q and −q: r₁ ≈ r − a cos θ, r₂ ≈ r + a cos θ (for r much greater than a). [1]
V = kq(1/r₁ − 1/r₂) = kq(2a cos θ)/(r² − a² cos²θ) ≈ kp cos θ/r², where p = 2aq. [1]
On the equatorial line θ = 90°, cos θ = 0 → V = 0 at every point. [1]
(ii) p = 3×10⁻⁹ × 4×10⁻³ = 1.2×10⁻¹¹ C m; V = kp/r² = 9×10⁹ × 1.2×10⁻¹¹/(0.2)² = 2.7 V. [1]
The equatorial line is an equipotential (V = 0), so no work is needed. [1]
items.orq:
(B) (i) State Kirchhoff's two rules. Use them to obtain the condition for balance of a Wheatstone bridge. [3m]
(ii) In a Wheatstone bridge, P = 4 Ω, Q = 8 Ω and R = 6 Ω, and the fourth arm contains a coil of resistance 36 Ω. What resistance must be connected in parallel with the coil to balance the bridge? [2m]
items.orans:
(i) Junction rule: the sum of currents entering a junction equals the sum leaving it (charge conservation). Loop rule: the algebraic sum of the potential changes around any closed loop is zero (energy conservation). [1]
Bridge ABCD with P in AB, Q in BC, R in AD, S in DC and galvanometer G between B and D. At balance I_g = 0, so the current I₁ in P also flows in Q and I₂ in R also flows in S. [1]
Loop ABDA: I₁P − I₂R = 0; loop BCDB: I₁Q − I₂S = 0. Dividing: P/Q = R/S. [1]
(ii) Required S = QR/P = 8 × 6/4 = 12 Ω. [1]
36x/(36 + x) = 12 → 24x = 432 → x = 18 Ω in parallel with the coil. [1]

items.q:
(A) (i) Define mutual inductance. Derive an expression for the mutual inductance of two long coaxial solenoids of the same length l, the inner one of radius r₁ with n₁ turns per unit length and the outer one with n₂ turns per unit length. [3m]
(ii) Two coaxial solenoids are each 0.5 m long. The inner one has radius 1 cm and 400 turns; the outer one has 1000 turns. Find their mutual inductance and the emf induced in the inner solenoid when the current in the outer one changes at 50 A/s. [2m]
items.ans:
(i) Mutual inductance M: flux linked with one coil per unit current in the other (N₂φ₂ = M I₁); equivalently, emf induced in one coil per unit rate of change of current in the other. [1]
Current I₂ in the outer solenoid gives a uniform field B = μ₀n₂I₂ inside it. Flux linkage with the inner solenoid = (n₁l)(πr₁²)(μ₀n₂I₂). [1]
M = μ₀n₁n₂πr₁²l (the same value is obtained by taking current in the inner coil). [1]
(ii) n₁ = 800 m⁻¹, n₂ = 2000 m⁻¹: M = 4π×10⁻⁷ × 800 × 2000 × π(0.01)² × 0.5 ≈ 3.16×10⁻⁴ H. [1]
|e| = M dI/dt = 3.16×10⁻⁴ × 50 ≈ 1.58×10⁻² V ≈ 15.8 mV. [1]
items.orq:
